fields.features_heading: What the Door Crew Needs Before Anyone Enters
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the waiver, the guardian and contact sections, and the tablet your door crew searches on a busy night.
fields.feature_1:
A QR code that opens the waiver in line

Print the code on a sign halfway down the queue. Guests sign on their own phones while they wait, and nobody holds up the door with a clipboard and a pen while the line backs up.
fields.feature_2:
Guardian signatures for anyone under 18

When the birth date puts a guest under 18, the form asks a parent or guardian to sign in their own name. Both signatures sit on the guest's record for the door check.
fields.feature_3:
Contact clauses only for guests who opt in

Guests choose the standard route or the contact route. Choosing contact adds clauses to initial, one for each kind of contact, and asks for a safe word that ends the scene.
fields.feature_4:
A list of every effect inside the haunt

List the effects guests will meet inside, such as strobe lights or a fog room. Each guest ticks a box to confirm reading the list and can leave a note for staff before entering.
fields.feature_5:
A door tablet that searches by last name

Door staff type a last name and see every guest in the party marked Signed with the time, or Waiting. Anyone still Waiting signs on the spot from the same QR code on their phone.
fields.feature_6:
Export the code to your own repository

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host the waiver app wherever your ticketing runs. Keep changing it by prompt, or hand it to a developer.

fields.usecase_heading: The Waiver at Four Different Haunts
fields.tab_content_1:
Six friends signed in line, all six on file at 8:14 PM

Kristof Moravec's party of six joins the queue at Gallowmoor Scare Farm on a Saturday night. Each friend scans the QR code on the queue sign and signs on their own phone. At the door, gate lead Pelagia Zelenka types Moravec into the tablet. All six names read Signed, the last one at 8:14 PM.
fields.tab_content_2:
Nyssa, 15, goes in after her mother signs as guardian

Nyssa Delacorte is 15 and in line for the Crowsend Fire Company haunted barn. Her date of birth opens a guardian section on the form. Her mother, Iolanthe Delacorte, signs it on the same phone in her own name. The door tablet shows Nyssa as Signed with a Guardian signed tag, and both signatures sit on her record.
fields.tab_content_3:
Opting into contact adds three clauses and a safe word

Guests at The Cinder Mill pick a route at the ticket window. Dragomir Sundqvist picks contact, so his waiver adds three clauses to initial, the first one allowing actors to touch him. He initials each and sets Lanterns as his safe word. His record tells the door crew to hand him a red glow necklace.
fields.tab_content_4:
Her waiver from 8:47 PM, with the incident note on it

A guest twisted an ankle at the hay-bale exit of Duskhollow Corn Maze at 9:30 PM. Operations manager Lettice Benedek searches Brisbois on the office tablet and opens Oriel Brisbois's waiver, signed at 8:47 PM on version 3 of the wording. She adds an incident note, which stays attached to that waiver.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Haunted House Waiver Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a haunted house waiver form, get the wording reviewed, and test it in the queue before opening night.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Walk the route and list every effect
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Set the routes and the age rules
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Have an attorney review the wording
fields.howto_step_1_des: Walk the route with a notepad and write down every effect a guest meets: strobe lights, fog, actors who grab, low ceilings, water. Each one goes into the risk section in plain words a guest can read on a phone.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide whether the haunt runs one route or adds a contact route. Set your own minimum age for each, and the age below which a guardian signs. Settle these before any wording, because the form branches on them.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Send the draft to an attorney licensed in your state before guests sign it. Whether a waiver holds up turns on its wording and on state law, and some states restrict waivers for minors. Ask about the guardian section on its own.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe the haunt, the routes, the guardian rule, and the door check in one prompt. Emergent builds the waiver, the database that stores each signed copy, and the door tablet screen. Change any part later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Print the QR code for the queue
fields.howto_step_5_des: Print the QR code on a sign partway down the queue, where guests stand still long enough to read. Add a second sign at the ticket window for walk-ups. Keep each clause short enough to read on a small screen.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Have five crew members sign as guests the night before opening, including one under 18 with a guardian and one on the contact route. Check each record on the door tablet and confirm the wording version beside every signature.
fields.howto_step_7_des: When the wording changes, save it as a new version and keep old signatures tied to the version their signer saw. Ask your attorney or insurer how long to keep the records, and leave them searchable by last name.

faq_plan.q: What is a haunted house waiver form?
faq_plan.a: A haunted house waiver form is a liability waiver a guest signs before entering a haunted attraction. A liability waiver is a legal document in which a participant acknowledges the risks of an activity and agrees not to hold the organizing party responsible if an injury or incident occurs. This one names the haunt's own effects.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a haunted house waiver form?
faq_plan.a: List your effects and routes, have a lawyer who practices where you operate review the wording, then describe the form in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form and a database that keeps every signed copy, and you change either one by prompting.

faq_plan.q: Which fields should a haunted house waiver form ask guests to fill in?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the guest's name, date of birth, and an emergency contact, then a dated signature under the release your attorney wrote. Add a guardian section for minors and a checkbox confirming the guest read the list of effects. The app Emergent builds saves every field of each signed copy to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can guests sign a haunted house waiver form before they arrive?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put the waiver link in the ticket confirmation, and guests sign at home before they drive over. Keep the QR code in the queue for walk-ups and anyone who skipped it. The same sign-ahead link suits a yoga waiver form that new students fill in before their first class.

faq_plan.q: How should a haunted house waiver form handle guests under 18?
faq_plan.a: Ask for a date of birth up front and require a guardian's signature for anyone under 18, signed in the guardian's own name. Set a separate minimum age for the haunt itself if you have one. Waivers for minors are limited in some states. Ask your attorney to review that section before opening night.

faq_plan.q: How do I add a contact route to a haunted house waiver form?
faq_plan.a: Add a route choice before the release. Guests who pick contact see extra clauses to initial, each describing one kind of contact in a sentence or two, and a field for a safe word. Emergent builds that branch from a plain-English description, and you change the clauses later by prompting.

faq_plan.q: What health questions belong on a haunted house waiver form?
faq_plan.a: Ask about the effects, not diagnoses. List each effect in the haunt in plain words, and have the guest confirm reading the list, with a free-text note for anything staff should know. The same approach works on a salon waiver form: list the products used and ask about reactions.

faq_plan.q: Should scare actors sign a haunted house waiver form too?
faq_plan.a: Yes, but give actors their own version, because their risks differ from a guest's: makeup, costumes, props, and long shifts in the dark. Collect it before the first rehearsal, keep it apart from guest records, and have your attorney review it.

faq_plan.q: How long should a haunted house waiver form take to sign?
faq_plan.a: Aim for under two minutes, about the time a guest spends between the queue sign and the door. Keep clauses to a few short sentences and put the signature last. Emergent can build it as a conversational flow with one question per screen, which reads well on a phone in the dark.

faq_plan.q: How is a haunted house waiver form different from a general release?
faq_plan.a: A haunted house waiver form names the attraction's own effects and contact rules, while a general liability waiver form covers an activity in broader terms. Start from the general release your attorney approves, then add the haunt's effects and any contact clauses on top.

This page shows the form working on a busy night: a group of six signing from a QR code in the queue, a 15-year-old whose date of birth opens a guardian section, a contact haunt where opting in adds clauses to initial and a safe word, and an operations manager pulling up one guest's signed waiver after a twisted ankle. Release wording goes to an attorney licensed in the operator's state; the form records who signed which version and when.
